summary: AI observability has become critical as LLM deployments scale, with the market growing to an estimated $2.69 billion in 2026 and projected to reach $9.26 billion by 2030 at a 36.2% CAGR. Without proper monitoring, teams face runaway API costs, degraded model outputs, and blind spots in multi-step agent workflows that are nearly impossible to debug. Gartner predicts LLM observability investments will account for 50% of GenAI deployments by 2028, up from just 15% in early 2026, underscoring how central these tools have become to production AI operations.

tools.name: LangSmith
tools.monitors: LLM traces, chain execution steps, prompt versions, evaluation runs, and agent reasoning paths primarily within LangChain and LangGraph ecosystems
features: Rich trace visualization with step-by-step chain debugging
Built-in evaluation and dataset management framework
tools.pricing: Developer tier free at 5,000 traces/month; Plus at $39/seat/month; overage approximately $2.50 per 1,000 traces. Estimated £80/month for 100K traces.
tools.best_for: Teams already using LangChain or LangGraph who need the richest debugging, evaluation framework, and prompt management tightly coupled to their orchestration layer

tools.name: Helicone
tools.monitors: LLM API requests and responses acting as a proxy gateway, tracking cost per request, latency, token usage, error rates, and model performance across providers
features: Proxy-based setup requiring minimal code changes (2-minute integration)
Best-in-class cost tracking and spend dashboards
Request caching to reduce redundant API calls
SOC-2 Type II and HIPAA compliance on Team tier
tools.pricing: Free Hobby tier at 10K requests/month; Pro at $79/month (unlimited seats, usage-based beyond included volume); Team at $799/month (compliance features); Enterprise custom pricing. Approximately £20/month for 100K traces, making it the most cost-effective managed option.
tools.best_for: Cost-sensitive teams wanting the simplest setup and best cost visibility across multiple LLM providers without heavy instrumentation overhead

tools.name: Weights & Biases (W&B) Weave
tools.monitors: LLM traces, experiment runs, model evaluations, dataset versions, prompt iterations, and end-to-end ML pipeline lineage from training through production inference
features: Unified experiment tracking and LLM tracing in one platform
Weave for LLM-specific tracing and evaluation
Integration with major LLM frameworks and providers
tools.pricing: Free tier available for individual use; Team plans start at $50/user/month; Enterprise pricing available on request. Usage-based compute charges apply for certain evaluation workloads.
tools.best_for: ML and research teams that need unified coverage from model training experiments through LLM production monitoring, especially those already invested in the W&B ecosystem

tools.name: Arize AI (Arize Phoenix)
tools.monitors: LLM spans and traces, retrieval quality in RAG pipelines, embedding drift, model performance metrics, and agent multi-step reasoning; extends long-standing ML monitoring into LLM workloads
features: RAG pipeline retrieval evaluation and ranking quality
Online evaluations with configurable LLM judges
Arize Phoenix open-source version for local use
Integration with existing ML monitoring infrastructure
tools.pricing: Phoenix is open-source and free to self-host. Arize managed platform offers a free Developer tier; Growth plans start around $200/month; Enterprise pricing on request with volume-based negotiation.
tools.best_for: Enterprise teams with existing ML monitoring needs who want a single platform spanning classical ML and LLM observability, especially those running RAG systems or needing deep embedding analysis

tools.name: Langfuse
tools.monitors: LLM traces, prompt versions, token usage, latency, cost per trace, user sessions, and custom evaluation scores across any LLM framework or provider
features: Prompt management with versioning and A/B testing
Custom score hooks for online and offline evaluations
Cost tracking by model, prompt, and user
SDKs for Python, JS/TS, and REST API
Integration with DeepEval and other evaluation libraries
tools.pricing: Cloud free tier for under 50K requests/month; paid cloud plans start at approximately £20 for 500K requests. Self-hosted is free with approximately £30/month infrastructure cost and 2 hours/month maintenance overhead.
tools.best_for: Teams wanting a framework-agnostic, OpenTelemetry-native tracing and prompt management solution that can be fully self-hosted for data privacy, with strong evaluation integration

tools.name: OpenLLMetry
tools.monitors: LLM calls, token consumption, latency, and errors via OpenTelemetry-standard instrumentation, sending data to any compatible observability backend such as OpenObserve, Jaeger, or Datadog
features: OpenTelemetry-native SDK requiring minimal code instrumentation
Automatic instrumentation for major LLM SDKs including OpenAI, Anthropic, and LangChain
Trace context propagation across distributed services
tools.pricing: Fully open-source and free; backend storage and visualization costs depend on chosen destination platform (e.g., OpenObserve self-hosted is free, cloud tiers vary).
tools.best_for: Teams that already have an OpenTelemetry-compatible observability stack and want to add LLM-specific instrumentation without vendor lock-in or adopting a new platform

tools.name: Confident AI (DeepEval)
tools.monitors: LLM output quality, hallucination rates, answer relevancy, contextual precision and recall in RAG pipelines, toxicity, bias, and 50+ additional evaluation metrics in production and CI/CD pipelines
features: Online observability layer with evaluation integrated at trace level
RAG-specific metrics including contextual relevancy and faithfulness
Used by OpenAI, Google, and Microsoft teams
tools.pricing: DeepEval open-source library is free. Confident AI managed platform offers a free tier; Pro plans start at $49/month; Enterprise pricing available on request.
tools.best_for: Teams prioritizing output quality and safety evaluation depth over infrastructure monitoring, particularly those building RAG systems or customer-facing applications where hallucination and relevancy are critical

cost_tips: Implement request-level caching using a tool like Helicone or a semantic cache layer so identical or near-identical prompts return stored responses rather than triggering new API calls, which can reduce costs by 20-40% for applications with repetitive query patterns

Set up token budget alerts and hard limits per user, feature, or environment in your observability tool so you catch cost spikes from prompt injection attacks, runaway agent loops, or unexpectedly long context windows before they result in large bills

Use model routing and tiering by directing simple classification or extraction tasks to cheaper, smaller models such as GPT-4o-mini or Haiku while reserving expensive frontier models only for complex reasoning tasks that demonstrably require them, auditing the split regularly using trace data

Optimize prompt templates using your observability tool's prompt versioning features to systematically trim system prompts and few-shot examples, as even reducing average prompt length by 15-20% across high-volume endpoints can produce significant monthly savings at scale
